reason: The text presents a rebellion against elite privilege rather than affirming it. The insurgents explicitly argue that 'all the congregation are all holy' (כָל־ הָֽעֵדָה כֻּלָּ֣ם קְדֹשִׁ֔ים) and question why Moses and Aaron elevate themselves above the community. The narrative depicts this as a challenge to the notion of inherent superiority. While the text ultimately shows God establishing a priesthood through Aaron, this is presented as divine selection and appointment rather than inherent superiority. The passage emphasizes that holiness and status derive from God's choice, not from any inherent quality of the elite.
